claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature BCC state.
Quenching Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from above 1500 °C produces or retains the high-temperature BCC state.
The high-temperature BCC state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is metastable.
Local atomic rearrangements, particularly Al clustering, reduce the nucleation barrier for ordering.
A rapid transformation to an ordered phase occurs when the thermodynamic driving force exceeds the nucleation barrier.
As temperature decreases, the free-energy difference between the BCC phase and a more ordered phase increases.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations facilitate atomic diffusion that lowers the kinetic barrier to nucleation.
Local compositional fluctuations such as Al-rich clusters can reduce the kinetic limitation enough to trigger phase transformation.
The transformation product may be a B2 or FCC phase.
The ordering transformation is sensitive to cooling rate.
Slower cooling permits sufficient atomic diffusion for the ordering transformation to occur near a threshold temperature.
Rapid cooling largely retains the high-temperature BCC diffraction signature.
Rapid quenching kinetically freezes atomic diffusion and ordering.
The nucleation barrier will show a sharp drop at a temperature between approximately 1350 °C and 1100 °C.
Under slow cooling, new diffraction peaks corresponding to ordered structures will emerge near the predicted threshold temperature.
Changes in diffraction peak positions and intensities can detect the proposed Al-rich short-range-order clusters.
Changing cooling rate or simulated diffusion kinetics will shift the transformation onset.
The proposed mechanism is limited to approximately 1350–1100 °C under inert-atmosphere conditions.
